key_insight: The paper shows that dialogue compression should be treated as a living, turn-by-turn process rather than a one-shot summary. By preserving and revising compressed memory across turns, a model can stay efficient without steadily losing important context.
problem_solved: It addresses the growing cost of multi-turn dialogue systems, where repeatedly attending to the full conversation becomes expensive and naive compression methods either drop important details or accumulate errors over time.
method: Analyzes how conventional context compression breaks down in long, evolving conversations and why errors compound across turns.
Introduces a context-driven incremental compression strategy that updates the compressed memory as each new turn arrives.
Enables cross-turn memory sharing and revision so earlier compressed information can be refined instead of permanently discarded.
impact: This matters for practitioners building chatbots and conversational agents because it can reduce inference cost while maintaining better long-range consistency. It is especially useful for long dialogues where efficiency and fidelity both matter.

paper_title: Context-Driven Incremental Compression for Multi-Turn Dialogue Generation
